title: Minimum Subarrays in a Valid Split
summary: Given an integer array, determine the minimum number of subarrays for a valid split where each subarray's first and last elements have a greatest common divisor greater than 1, and all elements are included exactly once.
statement: Given an integer array, determine the minimum number of subarrays for a valid split where each subarray's first and last elements have a greatest common divisor greater than 1, and all elements are included exactly once. If no valid split is possible, return -1. The greatest common divisor of two numbers is the largest integer dividing both without remainder, and a subarray is a continuous segment of the original array.
constraints: Partition the full array into contiguous nonempty subarrays.
A group is valid when the GCD of its first and last values is greater than one; interior values do not affect validity.
Return the fewest groups, or -1 when no complete split exists.
hints: Let dp[i] be the minimum valid groups covering the first i elements.
From every reachable start, try each possible group end.
When the two endpoint values have GCD above one, relax dp[end+1] by one group.
Every partition has a unique sequence of endpoints, all of which are examined, so the minimum relaxation is exact.
editorial: Every partition has a unique sequence of endpoints, all of which are examined, so the minimum relaxation is exact.

tests.explanation: Split as [2,6,3,4] and [3]; endpoint GCDs are two and three, so two groups suffice.
Every possible first group begins with 1 and has endpoint GCD one, so no valid split exists.
